text: Decision Log v11 is issued with no approval recorded, in Draft status.
why: This run is the D-RCV-60 realignment: no human approval step is available, the run must not stop for one, and the overlay records the missing status as an assumption.
read: The log is complete and may be cited by the architecture, requirements and story documents of this run; the approval is recorded afterwards by the owner of the log.
impact: A document that is cited as the decision source carries Draft status until the approval is recorded.

text: Every owner label that named an individual in v10 is replaced by the placeholder of Template and Rules §R9, and the role or organisation the same cell states is kept after the placeholder. No role is attributed to an individual.
why: Root AGENTS.md rule 4 forbids names of people in any output, and the Decision Log does not say which role each individual holds, so writing a role would invent one.
read: The owner of each of the fifteen open decisions named in CG-B-ARCH-DL-1 is unknown until the role is confirmed; the count, the earliest date and the decision IDs of each By owner row are unchanged.
applied_in: Open decisions column F (DL01, DL02, DL03, DL04, DL05, DL06, DL07, DL08, DL09, DL12, DL13, DL14, DL20, DL35, DL37) and By owner column A (twelve rows); note in A4 of both sheets
impact: Fifteen of 41 open decisions have no named owner in v11. The decision content, the date needed, the blocks and the if-late text are unaffected.

text: The amendment of D-RCV-36 T1 and T2 is read as: a case workflow runs on the Temporal task queue of the service that owns it (rwb-<short>, namespace rwb-recovery), and scheduled work becomes a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow in the owning service as that service is realigned, with JOB-05 kept behind the TimerScheduler port until Epic 3.
why: The mark of the amendment is required by the work package, and neither the Decision Log nor §R8.4 gives the amended wording. The reading is taken from the only sources above the log in R-PREC: Architecture v5 slide 41 (one task queue per service in namespace rwb-recovery) and slide 44 (Schedules in the owning service), with plan DP-10.
read: T3 to T10 of D-RCV-36 are unchanged; the Drools, rule-package and decision-log terms stand as written.
applied_in: Decisions taken, row D-RCV-36, Decision cell and What it means for the build cell; row D-RCV-60 clause (9)
impact: If the amendment is read differently, the workflow and schedule ownership of RWB-PLT-WF and every service workflow story changes.

text: The header date of v10, 15 November 2026, is read as the date the sheet text was last edited, not as the issue date of the version, and is carried into v11 unchanged.
why: D-RCV-36 in the same log is dated 16 November 2026, one day later than the header, and no source says what the header date means.
read: The v11 Read me carries 22 November 2026 as the version date; the v10 header text is quoted unchanged in the Open decisions sheet.
applied_in: Open decisions row 2 (unchanged) and Read me row 9
impact: If the header is an issue date, v10 was issued before one of its own decisions; the v11 chain of versions is unaffected.

text: DL44 to DL49 and D-RCV-60 are added to the sheet Decisions taken, dated 22 November 2026, with a role as the taker; they are not added to Open decisions, because this run settles them.
why: Template and Rules §R8.4 names them as decisions to add, and the sheet Open decisions holds only questions still open.
read: The taker of each row is the role that owns the change: the recovery tech lead with the solution architect for DL44 and D-RCV-60, the product owner for DL45, DL46 and DL48, the product owner with the IT lead for DL46, the recovery tech lead for DL47, and the business analyst with the solution architect for DL49.
applied_in: Decisions taken rows 28 to 34; Read me rows 12 and 16
impact: A reader who looks for DL44 to DL49 under Open decisions finds them under Decisions taken instead; the count in that sheet rises from 22 to 29.

text: A release date named inside a row carries (tentative); a date a decision is needed by does not, and no date is changed.
why: Rule 10 of the run and DL48 require every release date to be marked tentative and every date to be copied unchanged.
read: Four release references are marked: Epic 5 litigation in March 2027 (DL03), the Epic 1 release on 29 November (DL34) and the 30 November release (DL43, twice). The needed-by dates in column G keep the date picker format d mmm yyyy and are not marked.
applied_in: Open decisions E8, I39, C46 and I46
impact: If a release date moves, the row that names it is reissued; the mark is a statement of the source, not a new date.

text: The decision text of DL44 to DL49 is written out from the one-line entries of Template and Rules §R8.4, and the reading given to each is the run rule it states.
why: §R8.4 lists the six rows by name only, so the full sentence of each decision has to be written from the rule the row stands for.
read: No row adds a business rule, a value, an owner service or a date that the template, the run rules or Architecture v5 does not state; the service, table, endpoint, event, workflow and job owners quoted are those of the Microservice Ownership Map v1.
impact: A reviewer may want the six rows phrased as formal decisions; the substance is the rule set of D-RCV-60.

text: The By owner sheet keeps one row per v10 owner label, so the sheet still reads 31 owners and 41 open decisions; only the six rows of a label that named an individual change, and the description line of Decisions taken is updated from 22 to 29 because seven rows are added.
why: Rule 1 and the work package keep every number of the source, and the two counts are the only numbers that the added rows make wrong.
read: Every other count, earliest date and decision ID in the workbook is the v10 value.
applied_in: By owner A2 and A4; Decisions taken A2
impact: If the owner rows are merged by role later, the 31-owner count falls; that is a D1 register task, not this version.
